outcome: Store networks that configure themselves from a template and report what customers actually experienced, not just device counters.
overview: Retail network operations tend to be reactive because the network cannot describe itself: a store reports a problem, an engineer connects to a switch, and the diagnosis begins. Catalyst switching with Catalyst Center, or Meraki where cloud management suits better, changes what the network reports — configuration is pushed from a template and assurance data explains what a user actually experienced. The choice between the two management models is the real decision, and it turns on whether the chain wants an on-premises controller it operates or a cloud console it consumes.

benefits.text: Store network configuration is pushed from a template rather than assembled per site
benefits.limits: Template value depends on store formats being few; a chain with many formats gets many templates and proportionally less benefit

benefits.text: Assurance data explains what a user experienced instead of only what a device reported
benefits.limits: Assurance covers the vendor’s own equipment; a mixed access layer produces a partial picture that should be described as partial

benefits.text: A management model can be chosen per estate rather than imposed by the hardware
benefits.limits: The two management models are not interchangeable after purchase; the choice is effectively made at the hardware order

residency: On-premises management keeps assurance data inside the estate; cloud management sends telemetry to vendor-operated regions, and which model applies is a recorded design decision

notFor.situation: A chain already running a controller-based campus platform from another vendor
notFor.why: Assurance depth comes from the vendor owning the access layer; a mixed estate gets the console without the insight

notFor.situation: Stores with a handful of ports and no wireless requirement
notFor.why: Controller and assurance overhead exceeds the operational problem at that size

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Cisco implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to a proven pilot ring; rollout at an agreed stores-per-week rate
Support model: Vendor hardware and software support with a replacement term suited to store criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed network operations.
1) Assessment — format review, port and access-point density, current fault profile, management-model decision
2) Design — site templates per format, ring model, assurance baselines
3) Pilot — one store per format built from template with assurance validated
4) Roll out and hand over — chain rollout by ring, operations handed over
deliverables: A new store is brought live from its template without per-device configuration
Assurance reporting attributes a reported store issue to network, circuit or application
A template change reaches one ring and can be rolled back within the agreed window
